classification.difficultyReason: Calculate spending from the labelled percentages and explain why the larger percentage gives the smaller amount when the income bases differ; the earlier calculations scaffold this comparison.

inlines.text: The two pie charts shown below represent how two cousins, Michelle and Sarah, spent their monthly incomes from their part-time jobs.

spec.description: Sarah's pie chart; unequal labelled sectors require ordinary TikZ rather than the equal-sector fraction-circle template. Category fills are mapped consistently to the house palette; outlines and radii are black.
spec.mathematics: Clockwise from the upward radius: Clothes 25% (90 degrees), Food 20% (72 degrees), Cosmetics 15% (54 degrees), Going out 28% (100.8 degrees), Other 12% (43.2 degrees).
spec.answerVisibility: All category names and percentages are permanent supplied givens.

spec.description: Michelle's pie chart, at the same scale as Sarah's. Unequal labelled sectors require ordinary TikZ rather than the equal-sector fraction-circle template.
spec.mathematics: Clockwise from approximately upward: Clothes 27% (97.2 degrees), Food 19% (68.4 degrees), Cosmetics 15% (54 degrees), Going out 25% (90 degrees), Other 14% (50.4 degrees).
spec.answerVisibility: All category names and percentages are permanent supplied givens.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Suppose that in a particular month each girl earns $\$400$. How much money does each of the girls spend on clothes?

children.label: b
children.prompt: In the next month Michelle earns $\$400$ but Sarah earns $\$440$. How much money does each of the girls spend on clothes?

children.label: c
children.prompt: Comment on your answers to parts a and b.

answer.short: Michelle spends a higher percentage on clothes, but the amount also depends on each girl's income. Sarah spends more in part b.
answer.worked: With equal incomes in part a, Michelle spends $\$108$ and Sarah spends $\$100$. In part b, Sarah's higher income means that her 25% is $\$110$, more than Michelle's $\$108$. A higher percentage does not necessarily represent a larger amount when the totals differ.
